Those two are re-imported under their historical names because tests/test_h3_phantom_characters.py imports them from here, and a 54-case parity run against the pre-extraction function found no difference. The field reader still prefers the occurrence of each field that starts its own line (the validator counts fields that way, and reading them differently refused a prompt for missing a [Shot 1] it carried), and the refusal still prints the fields it found; the sentence it prints lives in services/director/h3_prompt_shape.py, so this file pays the call.

notes.app/wgp.py: New seam, two lines, opened because `model_mode` is a control whose type belongs to the model that declares it: YuE2 and the numeric image models write numbers, while the Qwen3 TTS models read the same field as a language and call `.lower()` on it. Studio keeps one params object across model switches, so a number chosen for music rode into a voice clone and cost the attempt -- measured: eight consecutive failures, each one instant, all of them `AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'lower'`, across Qwen3 Base, Voice Design and CustomVoice. The line is where settings are validated, so every path that generates sees the repaired value; the rule, and the reason a numeric control is left alone, live in app/services/tts_model_modes.py. Hooking validate_task instead would have missed the Gradio path, which reaches validate_settings directly.
notes.app/models/TTS/qwen3/pipeline.py: New seam, three lines, and the smallest that removes the crash: the import and the one line that turns 'is this text?' into an answer before `(model_mode or "auto").lower()` is reached. The model is the last reader of a value it does not own, so it degrades to its own default ("auto" for a language, the first supported speaker for CustomVoice) instead of raising. The rule is in app/services/tts_model_modes.py; no beam of it is repeated here.
notes.docs/TTS-Characters.md: New seam, one section, in the doc that describes exactly what a person is doing when they hit this: Studio -> Audio -> Speech -> voice cloning. It records the control's two meanings, the measured failure (eight attempts, ~8s each, `AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'lower'`), the two halves of the repair and why a numeric control must be left alone -- without it the next person reads the fix as an unexplained special case in the settings path. Trimmed to 25 lines for this seam; the long form belongs in app/services/tts_model_modes.py, which is ours.

notes..gitignore: One line, and the smallest seam here: app/writer_supervision.json is machine-specific (it holds the command that starts this machine's writer), so it must not be committed. Adding it to the ignore list is the only way to keep it out of the repository, and the line is a path, not code: a merge that takes upstream's side loses the ignore and shows the file as untracked, which is visible and harmless, unlike committing a local path. Raised from 1 to 2 for the same reason and the same kind of path: app/director_review_gate.json holds this machine's answer to 'stop after the shot images and wait for me', which is a preference rather than part of the project, and the alternative -- writing our setting into upstream's own config file -- would put a key upstream does not know about into a file it rewrites.
notes.launcher_profile.js: New seam, nine lines: rtx50Profile(), which asks for the RTX 50 runtime without the kernel's hardware inventory. Measured on this machine: two launches of the same app five minutes apart picked different runtimes because that inventory was empty on one of them, and the fallback is not neutral -- app/env carries the legacy CUDA 12.8 stack whose mmgp is 3.7.12, older than requirements.txt now requires (3.8.2), so the app stops on its own version check instead of starting. The addition is a three-line factory plus its comment; nothing else in the file changed.
notes.start.js: New seam, nine lines: a launch that was told nothing about the GPU prefers the RTX 50 environment when that environment's install marker exists, rather than the legacy environment that cannot import the required mmgp. It is written as a template expression so the check happens at launch, where the file system can answer it. The two cases that were already correct -- RTX 50 detected, and every non-RTX-50 profile with its own recovery path -- resolve exactly as before, verified by calling this module with three simulated kernels.
notes.app/services/director/planners/short_fil: Deliberate raise of one line, and the only one here. The H3 native shot-plan call asked for thinking_budget=None, which for a gemma-style writer resolves to 4096 (base.py) and therefore RECEIVES NO GRAMMAR: the schema is attached only when thinking is off, because the constraint has to apply from token 0. Measured consequence on a real run: a request for 16-22 shots came back as 37 and stopped on the 32000-token ceiling (finish=length, 148,599 chars), so the last shot was cut mid-object and the plan was rejected -- the repair pass in the same file already asked for 0. An argument cannot be extracted into a module, so the line is ours; reverting it restores the unconstrained first attempt.
notes.ui/src/App.tsx: Opened deliberately, for the assistant's floating panel: an import and one mount, in the app shell, because the assistant is meant to be reachable from every area -- the Studio, the Director, the Editor and the settings. The alternative was mounting it inside MainContent, which is ours and has two lines of slack, and that would have left the editor without it. Two adjacent lines are the smallest seam this repository can express, and if upstream rewrites the shell they are two lines to re-add.
notes.app/services/llm_guides/director/minimax: The prompt contract itself, so it has to be written where the planner reads it. Ours are two rules the compiled prompt enforces anyway: shot numbering restarts inside every clip (the film's eleventh shot is still [Shot 11] and [Shot 1] in its own body), and timestamps are local to the clip. Both are stated as short as they can be while keeping the literal [Shot 11] example -- the thing that taught the global number in the first place.
notes.app/models/minimax_h3/lora_affine.py: New seam, fifteen lines, and a ceiling raised instead of an extraction because the code that had to change is the guard itself. Upstream refuses to convert a LoRA whose AdaLN width differs from the checkpoint when the checkpoint table is not the canonical one to within 1e-5. Measured on the operator's fine-tuned H3 checkpoint (h3ErosMax beta5): the table is the same shape (1025x8) and drifts by 3.7e-4 relative, 9.9e-4 per element, so every 8-step Acc LoRA was refused and the checkpoint could not use one at all. The conversion already fits its map from the checkpoint's own table, which is the correct basis for that checkpoint, so the residual is a diagnostic and not an error: the ceiling is now 5e-3, a table that is not a pruned projection still fails (orders of magnitude above it), and a drift between the two prints what it measured instead of refusing. Pinned by tests/test_h3_lora_affine_tolerance.py, which also proves a genuinely incompatible table is still rejected.
notes.update.js: New seam, thirty lines, and a launcher script is the one place where extraction is not available: Pinokio reads the step list from this file, so the only way to decide an Update differently is to change the decision in place. What changed is the decision itself. Update used to skip the dependency install, the kernel step and the UI build whenever git pull said 'already up to date', which says nothing about the tree: a merge done outside Pinokio (an editor, an assistant, a hand-run git merge) leaves the pull with nothing to report while the code needs all three. Measured on this install after the 3.0.0 merge: Update printed 'Already up to date - Web Push runtime verified; skipped the full dependency install and UI rebuild' while requirements.txt had gained three pins and a new kernel installer, and that was harmless only because the environment had been verified by hand. Now the build path records the commit and the two dependency manifests it just satisfied in app/.maestro-runtime-stamp (a dotfile, already ignored by app/.gitignore's leading .* rule, so no ignore change), and the next Update compares against it through app/scripts/runtime_stamp.py (ours). Two steps are the minimum the engine allows: one run before the branch supplies the token, one run after the last install step writes it. The first Update after this lands on the build path on purpose, because no record exists yet. Pinned by tests/test_runtime_stamp.py, which proves a changed commit, a changed requirements.txt and an unreadable repository all report stamp-stale.
